Assessment of BA.evidence_source: Body appreciation, a more recently conceptualized measure of body image, goes beyond body evaluation to include respect for one's body, acceptance of one's body, favorable opinions of one's body, and the ability to reject unrealistic cultural expectations of women's bodies and appearance (Avalos, Tylka, & Wood-Barcalow, 2005).

section_summary.extract_value: The Introduction reviews literature comparing body image across sexual orientations, noting inconsistent findings and a gap in research including bisexual and queer-identified women. It defines body appreciation (citing Avalos, Tylka, & Wood-Barcalow, 2005) and states two hypotheses predicting higher body appreciation among sexual minority women (controlling for covariates) and lower body appreciation for bisexual women compared to other sexual minority women.
section_summary.evidence_source: This research report focuses on the potential relationships between sexual orientation and body appreciation, a multifaceted measure of positive body appraisal and evaluation, in a sample of adult women. We tested two hypotheses: (1) body appreciation would be higher for sexual minority women than heterosexually-identified women when controlling for age, BMI, sexual relationship status, and education level; and (2) body appreciation would be lower for bisexual women than other sexual minority women when controlling for sexual relationship status.
